cells.tense: You are still hoping, right now, and the hope is yours.
cells.verb: keep believing in something after everything that has tested it
cells.place: in what you carry forward with other people — the practices, the stories, the way things get done between you
cells.ask: take one piece of what you hope for and hold it steady under real weight — a schedule, a cost, a hard week — without gripping it; what comes back is a shared thing that shines because it actually grew, not because you willed it
cells.core:
You've been handed a lot and you're still handing it on, and you still believe in it. Not the untested kind of belief — the kind that has taken hits and is standing anyway. People can feel that when they pick up what you pass them: it isn't brittle. It has been leaned on.

What this is free to feed next is the practical side of the same strength. Hope that has lasted this long can bear real weight — a cost, a hard season, a thing that has to be kept going on a Tuesday when nobody is watching. Holding it that way, firm but not clenched, is how a shared thing stops being a wish and becomes something that actually grew.
cells.sheetLine: You still believe in what you pass on, and it shows in how it holds.

cells.tense: You are already standing in a future where this finally comes good.
cells.verb: keep hoping harder than the thing can bear
cells.place: in what you share with others — the practice, the tradition, the way you all agreed things mean something
cells.ask: before you say again that it will hold, sit with what you actually know about it — and let the part you don't know stay unknown for a while; what comes back is a shared thing that shines because it grew, not because you insisted
cells.core:
You're keeping the shared thing alive by sheer refusal to let it fail. Every gathering, every ritual, every conversation about it is you already living in the version where it finally lands with everyone — and you're bracing for that version so hard that nobody can tell you how it's actually going. The hoping has started doing the work the thing itself was supposed to do.

The way back isn't less faith. It's letting yourself know what you know before you declare it. Some of what you're carrying forward is real and some of it is wish, and you can feel the difference if you stop talking long enough. Hope that has checked itself against the room doesn't have to be shouted.
cells.sheetLine: You're insisting it will hold instead of checking whether it does.

cells.tense: The belief is behind you somewhere, and you're still standing at the spot where it used to be.
cells.verb: go through the shared motions with the hope drained out
cells.place: in what you keep carrying forward — the customs, the words, the things you still do together
cells.ask: pick one small practical piece of the shared thing and tend it with care — a meal made properly, a story told whole, a space kept ready — without trying to feel anything about it yet; what comes back is a shared thing that shines because it grew again under your hands
cells.core:
You're still doing it. The gatherings, the sayings, the things that mean something between you — you haven't dropped them. But the hope that makes them worth passing on is quiet right now, and what's left is the form with the fire turned low. Keeping the shape is not nothing. It's just not the same as believing in it.

The way back is not to make yourself hope again — that's pushing on an empty tank. It's to tend one real piece of it well. Care for the shared thing the way you'd care for a plant you weren't sure about: water it, give it light, don't clutch. Belief returns through what you actually do with the thing, not through trying to feel it.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping the practices with the hope gone quiet in them.

cells.tense: You are the one keeping it alive, right now, and you haven't said so.
cells.verb: carry a stubborn hope for the shared thing
cells.place: in what you pass on between you — the traditions, the common language, what everyone counts on being there
cells.ask: name one thing you keep going purely because you still believe in it — not because it's expected, not because it's tradition — and say that it's yours; what comes back is a shared thing that shines because you knew you grew it
cells.core:
The shared thing is still standing largely because you still believe in it. You show up, you keep the words alive, you hold the thread when others let it slack — and when anyone asks, you say that's just how it's done, that's what the tradition is. But traditions don't keep themselves. The persistence has a source, and it's you.

The way back is simpler than it sounds: notice what you're actually holding. Underneath the story about how it's always been done is a plainer fact — you keep this going because it matters to you, and you keep it going under real pressure. Owning that doesn't make it heavier. It lets the holding be firm instead of invisible.
cells.sheetLine: You're the reason it's still going. You call it tradition.

flags.detail: "you stopped believing" — a cell knows no one's past
